mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 5% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the GDP decline is accompanied by a simultaneous surge in industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered periods, or the unemployment spike is accompanied by a simultaneous acceleration in industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces earnings visibility and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the decline in industrial production is offset by a simultaneous surge in consumer spending proxies.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes earnings power, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment falls below 4% concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the coordinated rise is accompanied by a simultaneous spike in unemployment above 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the labor force participation rate (implied by a stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) over three consecutive months signals improved labor supply without rising unemployment, which enhances productive capacity and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable AND PAYEMS rising for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the labor force expansion coincides with a decline in industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a robust residential construction cycle, which boosts demand for materials and services and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the housing boom is accompanied by a simultaneous surge in mortgage rates above 7%.
